thesis: Repair measurement and emphasize valuable customer demand before expanding ad spend.
summary: Luis reports a profitable railing business heavily reliant on Google, with inconsistent CAC/LTV data and few repeat customers. Alex prioritizes attribution repair and a visible custom-order funnel for DIY customers: qualification, educational video, scheduled call and payment. He recommends periodic project/FAQ emails rather than forcing a subscription onto infrequent demand. At the roughly one-year check-in Luis reports revenue rising from 2.5 to 3.6 million and profit from 384,000 to 540,000, custom orders at half the business, three times the custom leads and a 20% close rate after price changes. He says unproductive campaigns were cut after attribution was fixed.

insights.title: Revenue alone does not identify productive ads
insights.explanation: The business reports making money while platform metrics imply losses. Alex recommends reconciling attribution before deciding which campaigns deserve more money.
insights.quote: we have numbers but they're not useful
insights.speaker: unresolved

insights.title: Lean into a differentiated customer use case
insights.explanation: DIY custom work is proposed because of existing demand and presumed lower price sensitivity. These assumptions require customer and margin data rather than universal application.
insights.quote: we're just basically leaning into the people that are the least price sensitive
insights.speaker: unresolved

insights.title: Match repeat marketing to the purchase cycle
insights.explanation: Rather than invent a railing subscription, he suggests maintaining awareness through project images and answers so buyers return when a real project arises.
insights.quote: I don't want to force continuity in this business
insights.speaker: unresolved

insights.title: Build the conversion path before adding traffic
insights.explanation: The sequence is to implement the custom funnel, expose entry points and add ongoing nurture, alongside delegated attribution work.
insights.quote: we have to have the system in place then we drive traffic to it
insights.speaker: unresolved

insights.title: Compare projections with the follow-up
insights.explanation: Luis reports 44% revenue growth and names custom orders and sales-process changes as important. This is evidence of a reported outcome, not proof of causal attribution or the earlier forecast.
insights.speaker: unresolved

review_status: Codex editorial draft; complete local transcript read; claims not independently verified
synthesis_method: Direct Codex extraction from complete local transcript; exact quotations verified locally
context_and_limits: These are owner-reported before/after numbers without independent accounts or a causal control. Reported revenue growth is 44%; profit growth from the figures is about 40.6%, with roughly unchanged 15% margins. This is below Alex's earlier 3–4x projection and 50–60% illustrative close-rate estimate. The follow-up briefly says 2.5 billion, inconsistent with the repeated million baseline. A hypothetical railing-resale-value report appears in a suggested script, not supplied evidence. The export ends mid-sentence.
review_changes: Adds the actual follow-up and distinguishes reported improvement from forecasts, flags attribution uncertainty, and preserves the explicit decision not to force recurring purchases.
